segments.text: to such a yogi who is established, who is established in this kind of yoga, this kind
of wonderful state of joy, to him, yichā shaktir umā-kumāri, his desire, his will
is energy, energy of Lord Shiva. Not only energy, umā, his will is called umā, and his will,
he is nominated as umāri. These three names he has put for his will, for the will of
satcha yogi. His will is energy of Lord Shiva, his will is umā, and his will is umāri. Now
he commentates on these three words. Yogi na parabhairavatāṁ samāpanaseya yā yichā sā shaktir umā-paraya
papāra-mēshiri, sātindra-rupa, sāja-kumāri, visu sarga-samhar-kṛda-parā, kumāra-kṛda-yā
mīdipātāṁ. Yogi, who is established, who has taken the establishment with Supreme
Bhairava, parabhairavatāṁ samāpanaseya. For satcha yogi, who has become one with Supreme
Bhairava, who has attained the full entry in the state of Bhairava. Yogi na parabhairavatāṁ
samāpanaseya. Yā yichā, his mere will, desiring, his energy, and his umā, his will is
energy of Lord Shiva, and his will is one with umā-parvati. That parvati doesn't mean the wife
of Lord Shiva, parvati means, parāya-pār-mēshiri, sātindra-rupa. Independent energy of Supreme
Lord is umā. Now he translates, kumāri. What kumāri means? Kumāri means, visu sarga-samhar-kṛda-parā.
That energy, who plays in the universe, in creating, protecting, and destroying it, because
the word kumāri is meant in grammar for play. Kumāri means the one, that energy, who is always
given to play. Kumāri, kṛda, yes. Kumāra, kṛda, yam. No, kṛda, yam, yin, kṛda.
Yin, meaning of kṛda. Kumāri is said yin, meaning of kṛda. Otherwise there is another way
to explain what kumāri is. Kumāri is the kumāri. Kumāri is in two ways. He is explaining
kumāri, the word kumāri. Kum means, bēdo, tāpika, māyābhumi. The differentiated perception
in this world is kum, differentiated person, perception. And that differentiated perception,
marīatī, that energy, who destroys that differentiated perception in this world, and
sentences, sentences, that differentiated perception in one's own nature. That is kumāri. There is
another way to explain what kumāri is. Kumāri is a par anubhubu gā. Kumāri means virgin.
Virgin means that girl who is not enjoyed by any other agency, who has established her own
nature in the state of enjoyer. She is enjoying her own nature in her own way. She does not require
any other agency for enjoyment. That is kumāri. That is the state of being virgin. So bhaktray
kātmī and sufranti. So that kind of girl is always one with her own nature, not looking
for other opposite sex. There is another way to explain what kumā means. Athva, yatā
umā kumāri parinata sarva-sanga, maheśarā kātmī sadāna arādānaya nitu dhukta, tātā
vāsī ca. Just as umā kumāri, the virgin kumāri, at the time when she was virgin, parinata
sarva-sanga. She was detached from all sides in the world of enjoyment and her mind was sentenced
to Lord Shiva only. Then she had given herself her penance to receive the blessings of Lord
Shiva. And she was always one with that being of Shiva. In the same way, tātāva, I say,
itchā. In the same way, the desire of such a yogi is like that. The desire he doesn't desire,
he doesn't will any other object. He will always entry in his own nature. Yati asmāt guru
bir itham yé vipāto dhristu vya khyātāstya. This is what our masters have explained, the
meaning of umā kumāri. Añā istu shaktit tamā yeti pati tta, yān kreya pēkho asya prakarsho vya khyātā.
Some other commentators of this Shūsūtras have explained, have commented, shaktir umā in
place of shaktir umā, they have kept shaktit tamā. In that way, if you explain that shaktit tamā
means, his will is filled with knowledge and action. Yān kreya pēkho asya prakarsho vya khyātā. This
is the desire of yogi is filled with energy of knowledge and energy of action. Yān kreya pēkho
asya prakarsho vya khyātā. His desire is pertaining to knowledge and action. Avam nēlau ke kawata asya yoginā
sthu leh ca. So, just like ordinary people, this kind of yogi does not possess gross desire
in his mind. Aptu, on the contrary, pārā shaktir upāya sarvatra apre dhātā, his energy of will
is always spring energy of Lord Shiva, one with spring energy of Lord Shiva. And so, hence,
Sarvatra apre dhātā, his will is never blocked by any power. Blocked are stopped by any power.
Tadoktam shriva satschandhi. Satschandhi sastra also says the same thing in this shloka. Sādevi,
Sarvadevi, nām, nām rūpa Ṭtishtati, yog māya prityacchana, kumāri, loku bāvini. His energy is one
with devi, and that devi is nominated in various ways of one energy of Lord Shiva, sātantra shakti.
And his energy of will is thus yog māya prityacchana, is concealed with the magic of yoga.
And he is nominated as kumāri, and his will is so loku bāvini, desired by every of every being.
Everybody wants such will, so that he wills and he gets it.
In Naitr Tantra also the same is explained. Sā māmeh chāpara shaktir avyukta sabāvaja,
ol opārvati, his will is my own will. His will is one with my own will, and supreme energy of mind,
and is avyukta, one with myself sabāvaja, and rises from my own nature.
It doesn't rise from senses. His will does not rise from senses. His will rises from the nature of being of Lord Shiva.
Vahineer Ushmev viggeya, Rasmi Rupa Ravariva, Sarvasi Jagatova, Pisa, Shakti, Karanathmika,
this energy of the will of yogi has become the cause of the whole universe, because that energy of yogi
is one with the energy of Lord Shiva, just as heat is one with fire, rays are one with sun.
In the same way, his energy is one with the self of Shiva.
This is concluded in Spanda in this Shloka.
He does not infuse power of will in his senses, but he wills and that is done.
He does not crave for that desire, and he desires, he wills and that is done, because he possesses the strength of supreme
Aay, Tātangbala Sperśā, Aay, Tātangbala Sperśā, this strength of supreme Aay.
